After eating a hearty brunch at Butterfinger Pancake, my favorite brunch restaurant, I went for a walk to digest my food and ended up at GS25 floating on the Han River. Let's be honest, I needed something to tone down the rich, buttery taste of brunch, and what's better than a warm bowl of ramen? Ramen cannot be missed in the Han River, right?

This GS25 is hidden a little away from Apgujeong, right next to the entrance to the tunnel that goes down to the river. The tunnel itself is quite amazing, and the long stretch of colorful graffiti art makes it feel like a secret gallery. It’s already a special experience in itself even before you reach the river.

I looked at Gangbuk across the river, feeling the wind, holding ramen in my hand. The scenery was really beautiful. The city skyline sparkles in the sunlight and the gently rippling river. The combination of simple food, street art, and priceless scenery doesn't get any better than this. It's one of those small but perfect moments you can experience in Seoul.

What is the difference between Tteokgalbi bibimbap and the same vegetable bibimbap in which the Tteokgalbi is broken up?
The rest of the ingredients look the same
I think that if you put the tteokgalbi from the set meal into the bibimbap from the set meal, it would be the same as the tteokgalbi bibimbap.
No, I think it is highly likely that the amount of tteokgalbi will be smaller. Of course, I've never seen it put in in the kitchen, so it's just a subjective feeling.
Anyway, it's a similar menu, but if you want to experience the original taste of delicious tteokgalbi, I think it's better to just order the set meal.
The portion size is a bit too big for adult men to eat.
Looks like enough for women to eat
And I don't know if it's because it's busy, but the service seems to vary depending on the seat.
It's not that I'm unfriendly or anything, but it's a bit disorganized and feels like a novice.
They didn't even give us water so we had to ask for it while we were drinking.
There was no brazier for the tteokgalbi at our table, but when we came out, everyone was serving tteokgalbi on a brazier.
I felt bad because I felt like we were the only ones who didn't receive the service we had to pay for.
The waiting isn't that bad, but it's very slight.
As of Friday lunch, no more than 10 minutes
I think if the service was more efficient, there would be almost no waiting time.

To summarize
Tteokgalbi tastes good
The amount is not large (for men)
Just order the tteokgalbi set meal.
The service still feels disorganized.
The waiting isn't too bad (less than 10 minutes).

But the tteokgalbi is delicious so I give it 5 stars.

Review of Daesam Restaurant in Yeouido 😊🥩

It was a place that came to mind when I wanted to eat neatly grilled meat in Yeouido 😋 As soon as I entered, I felt good because the store was spacious and well-organized, and the spacing between tables was not stuffy, so it would be comfortable for gatherings 🪑✨ Above all, there was good ventilation at each table, so I was less worried about the smoke that is typical of meat restaurants 💨👍

The basic setting was also presented neatly 🍽️ There were plenty of vegetables to wrap such as lettuce and perilla leaves 🥬 garlic 🧄 and sauces were also prepared so it was easy to combine them to suit your taste 😆 The side dishes overall had a clean taste, and the green onion salad in particular was perfect to eat with meat 🥢💚

Just looking at the meat, I was excited because it was beautifully marbled 🥩✨ As soon as I put it on the grill, I was excited by the sizzling sound 🔥😍 It was easy to grill because it was set up to prevent excess oil from splattering, and I was satisfied because it felt juicy as I cooked it one piece at a time and ate it right away 🤤💕

It was comfortable because the staff responded at exactly the right time 😊 I was able to ask for water or additional side dishes without pressure, and the overall store management felt good, so I enjoyed the entire meal 🧼✨

If you summarize it in one line:
Clean store 🏠 + Pleasant ventilation 💨 + Satisfied with the basic menu 🥬🧄 + Meat quality exceeds expectations 🥩💯
If you are looking for a comfortable place to eat meat in Yeouido, I think it would be a good idea to give it a try 😄🍀

A Japanese ramen restaurant that operates in New York has opened in Yeouido. I visited when it first opened.

I went to the address, but be careful because it's not easy to find because it's on the side rather than the front of the building!

Although it is a ramen restaurant, it has a modern rather than Japanese atmosphere. These days, many ramen restaurants in Japanese office buildings have this feeling, but it is as good as New York. ^^

There are two types of draft beer, 500cc and 300cc. I started by drinking a refreshing glass of 300, which is comfortable for lunch.

Tsukemen seems to be the main dish, and there are three types: basic, spicy, and yuzu. I had a hard time deciding, but I chose the basic!

The thickness of the noodles didn't give off a greenish smell and it maintained some moisture, so it went well with the deep texture of tsukejiru.

One thing that is disappointing is that there is no seaweed in the toppings, and it would be nice if pepper, vinegar ichimi, spicy pesto, etc. were prepared so that you can eat them according to your taste.

The ebi karaage (fried shrimp) was also very delicious.

The lunch set menu is good value for money.

The atmosphere is so good that I want to come for a drink in the evening.
I wanted to try a variety of menus, but due to circumstances I was visiting alone, so I'll have to try other menus I'm curious about next time!

reviews.author: Yunah Hahn
reviews.text:
While shopping, it was lunch time.
Sat down without waiting on a Saturday. Two Kaisen dongs.

Obok Fisheries, Ilpoom I live in Yeouido and go there often, so I thought Unido, which I had only heard about because it was a very hot place, would be just as good. Reviews say it is more expensive than Oboksusin, but it works well, but I think differently. The Kaisendon, which was seasoned with spicy tuna and meat sauce, was not very attractive because I didn't eat it, and eating it with poached rice later didn't have any special appeal either. The most important thing is the quality of the sashimi. At Obok Fisheries, scallop and amaebi are sweet, but here, they are non-o. Also, mid tier tuna is used. The seaweed was also not of fragrant quality seaweed. I received a refill of miso soup and ate two bowls, and both were lukewarm. A smile filled only with fried tofu. It wasn't a Kaisendon that was serious about quality and sashimi. Also, the atmosphere is open, like a department store food court, so it is a bit noisy and messy.

If you're looking for authentic Kaisen Dongul with classic fish quality, this isn't the place, but if you like the concept of Kaisen Dong topped with various things and a poached egg, and prefer a taste like spicy tuna and spicy sauce, I guess why not.
